text:
olivia: quick noteb7 spun up krypton20b (int4) in the experimental canary cluster. Short prompts look great, but we're seeing memory fragmentation / occasional OOMs on multi-turn chat traces.
sam: can you share the exact canary config and an example failing trace?
olivia: config dump: 
```
model: krypton20b
precision: int4
batch: 10
max_new_tokens: 400
slot_reserve: 0.05
packing_window: 192
kv_prefetch: true
compact_slot_on_idle: false
swap_threshold: 0.0
```
example failure: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.8 GiB" (seen ~2x in 50 runs, both on long-chat tests).
rahul: int4 + large packing windows amplify slab fragmentation; combination with high slot_reserve eats headroom. try smaller packing_window and aggressive compaction.
mei: also try lowering max_new_tokens to 128 for the default canary route and keep an investigator route with 400 for power users. small tradeoff in tail quality but big win for stability.
sam: ran quick permutations on canary host (same seed traces):
- A (baseline): max_new_tokens=400, batch=10, packing=192 -> 2 OOMs/50 runs, p95 latency 1.45s
- B: max_new_tokens=128, batch=10, packing=192 -> 0 OOMs, p95 1.52s, ROUGE-L delta vs fp16: -1.2
- C: max_new_tokens=400, batch=6, packing=128 -> 0 OOMs, p95 1.62s, throughput down ~18%
- D: max_new_tokens=256, batch=8, packing=128, compact_slot_on_idle=true -> 0 OOMs, p95 1.58s, ROUGE-L -0.6
rahul: interesting. compact_slot_on_idle helps a lot. can you try tensor-swap for cold tensors (swap_threshold=0.35) and also toggling int8-fallback?
olivia: kicked off overnight sweep with two branches: tensor-swap on + int8-fallback disabled, and tensor-swap on + int8-fallback enabled. also added a microbenchmark that simulates 30-turn chats with many short messages to exercise KV churn.
ci-bot: sweep queued: job_id=canary-sweep-540999-01, compare branches: int4(128)+compaction, int4(256)+swap, int4(256)+swap+int8-fallback.
mei: baseline eval numbers (from small eval run): fp16 ROUGE-L 44.2, EM on QA 72.4.
ci-bot: quick results (partial):
- int4(128)+compact: ROUGE-L 43.1, EM 71.0, tokens/s 3800, p95 latency 1.6s
- int4(256)+compact+swap: ROUGE-L 43.6, EM 71.6, tokens/s 3600, p95 1.9s
- int4(256)+swap+int8-fb: ROUGE-L 43.9, EM 72.0, tokens/s 3450, p95 2.1s
rahul: tradeoffs look reasonable. perf wins for int4(128) but quality recovers when using swap+int8-fallback at cost of tail latency.
sam: ops action items proposed:
1) set canary default max_new_tokens=128 for krypton20b-int4 routes
2) enable compact_slot_on_idle=true on canary int4 hosts
3) enable a toggle for tensor-swap per host pool (default off for hosted customers)
4) add targeted CI test: 30-turn short-message chat to detect fragmentation regressions
5) keep an 'advanced' route allowing max_new_tokens>=400 behind an opt-in flag and telemetry.
olivia: +1 to all. i'll open onboarding ticket with logs and the sweep configs and draft rollout notes for product.
ci-bot: created ticket INF-7890: krypton20b int4 canary frag sweep. linked artifacts: canary-sweep-540999-01 logs, microbench traces, config diffs.
mei: one more idea: add a runtime heuristic that reduces packing_window when live memory headroom < 6GB for int4 hosts. avoids OOMs automatically.
rahul: yes, nice. file a follow-up RFC for that heuristic and maybe a graceful degradation mode.
olivia: end-of-thread: will monitor sweep results tomorrow and propose defaults for canary -> staging rollouts. thanks all :rocket:
